analysis:
This is a provider lifecycle reliability change with no change to the coordinator, attestation, encryption, billing or App Attest paths.

Changes reviewed:
- LaunchAgent.restartAfterDrain (LaunchAgent.swift) now polls launchctl print until the old job is released, with a 60s bounded timeout, before bootstrapping. A job that is never released still ends in a bounded wait and a bootstrapFailed error.
- New ServiceDrain.relaunchDrainedProvider (ServiceDrain+Relaunch.swift) re-arms the watchdog via defer on both success and failure. RestartCommand.swift and UpdateCommand.swift both use it. Previously a failed relaunch left the watchdog disabled. The watchdog uses kickstartIfLoaded, which only acts on a loaded job, so it cannot resurrect an intentionally stopped provider. This relates to T-043 only in that crash recovery is preserved.
- LaunchctlControl.swift adds TaskLocal test seams (runnerForTesting, homeDirectoryForTesting). Production never binds them. They are task-scoped, with no environment or file-based activation path, so I found no new attack surface.
- The new tests exercise the relaunch path with a fake launchd and a fake home directory.

Minor observations that did not rise to findings:
- In UpdateCommand.swift the watchdog is re-armed before the catch block calls cancelPendingCandidateAttempt. A brief window exists in which the watchdog could act on a pending candidate. This is speculative and I did not see the watchdog or updater internals.
- loadService re-enables the job with launchctl enable, so a concurrent `darkbloom stop` during the up-to-60s wait could be overridden. This is pre-existing behaviour and presumably guarded by the drain lease, which was not supplied.

No threat-model assets (A-001..A-017) or boundaries (TB-001..TB-011) are affected.
